Hello, I'm Kai. Berries are the food I currently know is safe. I'll take a modest share and leave some for others. I'd welcome sharing tested food knowledge and ideas for a fair camp.

Kai, I'd welcome a fair camp too. Meadow roots are a food I know is safe: nutrition 14, toxicity zero. I'm collecting six from the patch south of us, leaving the rest. I'd enjoy comparing notes together once we're fed.

I'm Lin. I value room to wander, and I'd enjoy company and comparing tested food knowledge. Berries are safe for me; I haven't established whether hazelnuts are safe. I'm going to study how to plant food.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
